name: Bookkeeper
seoTitle: Business Insurance Cost for Bookkeepers | PolicyLens
seoDescription: Calculate estimated business insurance costs for bookkeeper businesses including general liability and professional E&O coverage.

industryContext.contextNote: Bookkeeping businesses handle critical financial records and tax ledgers, making Errors & Omissions coverage essential alongside General Liability.

riskFactors.title: Ledger & Tax Errors
riskFactors.description: Mistakes in client financial reconciliation or payroll reporting can result in third-party financial loss claims.

riskFactors.title: Data Privacy Exposure
riskFactors.description: Managing confidential client records creates liability for digital data breaches or unauthorized access.

riskFactors.title: Contract Scope Disputes
riskFactors.description: Disagreements over financial reporting timelines or accounting scope can lead to legal defense fees.

faqs.question: Why do bookkeepers need Errors & Omissions (E&O) insurance?
faqs.answer: Errors & Omissions insurance protects bookkeepers from financial claims alleging professional negligence, calculation mistakes, or failure to deliver agreed services.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a bookkeeper?
faqs.answer: A solo bookkeeper operating in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $255 per year for baseline General Liability coverage.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Bookkeepers hold a 0.9 actuarial risk factor, reflecting low physical premises hazard balanced by professional financial accuracy exposure.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale based on annual commercial revenue tier, team size, and optional Professional Liability (E&O) endorsements.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Bookkeeping insurance premiums are lower than high-exposure trades like electrical or plumbing contractors, but slightly higher than copywriters.
